category: disposable email alias and forwarding service (defunct)

free_tier.stated: a free email alias, valid for a chosen period from 12 hours to 3 months, forwarded to the user's real address; usable as often as the user likes
free_tier.notes: The offer was historical: the service stopped accepting new aliases on 31 March 2015 and stopped forwarding after that date.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no first-party message size limit appears on the archived pages; the service forwarded mail to a real address rather than storing objects

retention.stated: each alias lasted for a period the user chose, from 12 hours to 3 months; forwarding ended after 31 March 2015
retention.notes: The retention period was per alias and user-selected, not a single fixed number, so days is null.

egress.terms: not applicable: a receive-and-forward alias service, not a traffic egress offer

interface_detail: the archived first-party pages document a web signup form and a control panel, with no API, CLI or documented protocol
tooling: a web browser: the archived site offered a signup form and a control panel
chaining: a receive-and-forward alias with no documented API, so it offers no programmatic inbox to chain into an automated flow

limits.value: no new aliases created after 31 March 2015
alias validity from 12 hours to 3 months, chosen by the user

binding_note: new alias creation was closed on 31 March 2015, so the write gate binds before the 12-hour to 3-month alias lifetime does

identity_cost.detail: the archived signup help asks the user to type a current email address as the forwarding destination, solve a captcha and activate the alias by clicking a link in a confirmation mail; no card or phone is asked for

reliability_note: the service shut down on 31 March 2015; mailexpire.com now serves a domain-for-sale listing rather than the original service
confidence_note: first-party archived pages from 2012 to 2015 and the current mailexpire.com page were captured and quoted; no probe was run because the service no longer runs

evidence.quote: So, as of today, I am no longer offering the facility to create new mailexpire aliases.
evidence.proved: the first-party shutdown notice states that new alias creation ended

evidence.quote: Any existing aliases will continue to work as normal until the end of March. After that, no further mails will be forwarded.
evidence.proved: the first-party notice states that forwarding stopped after March 2015

evidence.quote: Remember. Alias forwarding will stop after March 31st 2015.
evidence.proved: the first-party notice fixes 31 March 2015 as the end of forwarding

evidence.quote: After payment is completed for MailExpire.com, we’ll guide you through the best available transfer option based on the domain’s current registrar and extension.
evidence.proved: mailexpire.com now serves a domain-for-sale listing, not the original service

evidence.quote: For a period you choose, from 12 hours to 3 months, anything sent to this email alias will be passed on to you at your actual email address.
evidence.proved: the alias ran 12 hours to 3 months and forwarded to the user's real address

evidence.quote: mailexpire is free, and you can use it as often as you like.
evidence.proved: the offer was free and repeatable

evidence.quote: Type your current email address into the "current email address" field. Any mail sent to your new alias will be sent to this address.
evidence.proved: the archived signup asks for an email address as the forwarding destination

evidence.quote: In order to protect ourselves, we've had to introduce a captcha test to the signup process.
evidence.proved: the archived signup page applied a captcha gate

evidence.quote: Your new mailexpire alias will now be prepared, but it will not be activated until you click on the control panel in the confirmation mail sent to you.
evidence.proved: activation required clicking a link in a confirmation mail

notes: Defunct receive-and-forward alias service. New alias creation and all forwarding ended on 31 March 2015 per the first-party shutdown notice. The archived pages document a web form and a control panel, with no API. mailexpire.com now serves a domain-for-sale listing.
